claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers under sustained loading is governed by the interplay of severe lattice distortion, short-range order, and nanoscale interfaces.
Severe lattice distortion, short-range order, and nanoscale interfaces modify dislocation dynamics relative to conventional metallic multilayers.
Interface-mediated creep is the dominant deformation mechanism in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
The proposed initial multilayer has pristine, well-defined interfaces and minimal pre-existing dislocation density.
An elevated temperature can activate creep while preserving the nanoscale multilayer structure.
The selected temperature and stress activate diffusional and interface-related deformation without causing coarsening or full recrystallization.
Nanoscale interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interfaces modified by compositional complexity and lattice distortion enhance localized diffusion.
Interfaces modified by compositional complexity and lattice distortion promote dislocation nucleation.
The distorted lattice and ordered local chemical environments hinder conventional dislocation glide.
Hindered dislocation glide promotes stress concentration at multilayer interfaces.
Interfacial stress concentration preferentially activates localized interface sliding.
Interfacial stress concentration preferentially activates diffusion-assisted dislocation nucleation and annihilation.
The proposed interface-mediated processes progressively accommodate plastic deformation.
HEA multilayers rely more strongly on interface-localized deformation than conventional metallic multilayers.
Sustained loading will produce increased dislocation pile-up density at and near interfaces.
Sustained loading will produce evidence of enhanced diffusion along interfaces.
Sustained loading will produce a non-uniform deformation profile with strain localization.
Plastic deformation under sustained loading in conventional metallic multilayers is primarily controlled by bulk-layer dislocation glide, with only minor interface-mediated contributions.

A lack of significant differences in creep behavior, interface-localized deformation, dislocation accumulation, and diffusion activity between ordered- and disordered-interface samples would falsify the proposed interface-control hypothesis.
